title: A fast chaser with momentum can fly through its target during its wind-up
observation: A small pursuer moving at over 300 studs/s started its 0.3 s attack wind-up when close to a boat while steering at a point slightly ahead of it. Every strike missed. Summary numbers (closest approach 1 to 2 studs) suggested it should have hit; a frame-by-frame probe of its state and distance showed it passing through the boat during the wind-up and arriving 28 studs past when the strike was checked. Locking the attacker onto the target and matching its speed during the wind-up made strikes land against a steady target while a target that boosted away still escaped.
recommendation: During an attack's tell, have a fast chaser hold onto its target (aim at the target, match its speed) rather than carry momentum toward a lead point, so the tell is the dodge window and not a coin flip. When an attack never lands, log the attacker every frame through the tell before tuning numbers.
applies_when: A kinematic or physics chaser has momentum and a wind-up before a contact attack
An attack's hit rate is near zero even though the attacker gets very close
limits: One game's kinematic sea pursuers, measured in Studio with a test autopilot as the target
Whether the locked-on wind-up feels fair to players is untested by people

evidence.detail: Sections 7 and 11 and bug 4 in section 22: the Echo's strikes all missed until its tell locked on; afterwards it hit a cruising boat twice in 13 s and missed a boosting one.
